ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a circle with B as the center, and C, G, F, D, A are on the circle. CG is a vertical diameter, and AD is a slanted diameter. The central angle between radii BG and BF is labeled 35°, and the central angle between radii BC and BD is labeled 55°. Reasoning: The problem asks for m\widehat{GCF}, which is the arc from G to F passing through C, so it is not the shorter arc GF at the lower right, but the corresponding major arc. From the central angle ∠GBF = 35° in the figure, the measure of minor arc GF is 35°. The whole circle is 360°, so the measure of major arc GCF passing through C is 360° - 35° = 325°.

raw_record.question_text: $\overline{AD}$ and $\overline{CG}$ are diameters of $\odot B$. Find $m\widehat{GCF}$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a circle centered at B with radii drawn to C, G, and F. The image shows the central angle ∠GBF marked 35°, so the minor arc GF measures 35°. The requested arc \widehat{GCF} is the arc from G to F that passes through C, i.e., the major arc GF rather than the small bottom-right arc. Use the full circle measure 360° and subtract the minor arc: m\widehat{GCF}=360°−35°=325°.
